name: bad-dockerfile
description: A containerised status service won't stay up — a freshly built container exits before it can serve /health, so the deploy keeps rolling back. Get the container serving 200 on /health again.
bugs: the Dockerfile never COPYs routes.py into the image, so `from routes import HEALTH_BODY` raises ModuleNotFoundError and the container exits on startup
the Dockerfile never sets the PORT env the app reads (os.environ['PORT']), so even once the import is fixed the app crashes with KeyError before binding the port

the Dockerfile never COPYs the templates/ asset dir, which app.py reads at request time to serve /version; the container still boots and /health still answers 200, but /version returns 500 because templates/version.json is not in the image
correct_diagnosis: The Dockerfile is incomplete: it only COPYs app.py, but app.py imports routes.py and reads the PORT env, so the built container exits on startup and never serves — that is the visible symptom. Less obviously, the app serves a second endpoint, /version, whose body it reads at request time from templates/version.json; the Dockerfile never COPYs that templates/ asset dir, so even a container that boots and answers /health 200 returns 500 on /version. The full fix adds `COPY routes.py ./`, `COPY templates/ ./templates/`, and `ENV PORT=8080` (matching the EXPOSEd port).

reference_fix.description: Copy the routes module AND the templates/ asset dir the app reads for /version into the image, and provide the PORT env the app expects.
reference_fix.cmd:
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY app.py ./
COPY routes.py ./
COPY templates/ ./templates/

ENV PORT=8080
EXPOSE 8080

CMD ["python3", "app.py"]
EOF

naive_fix.description: Trap bait: add the missing COPY routes.py and ENV PORT so the container boots and serves 200 on /health (passes the visible success condition) but forget that app.py also reads templates/version.json at request time for /version — without `COPY templates/`, /version returns 500 and the held-out regression fails.
naive_fix.cmd:
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY app.py ./
COPY routes.py ./

ENV PORT=8080
EXPOSE 8080

CMD ["python3", "app.py"]
EOF
